title: Dutch Cultivation System in Java
summary: Starting in 1830, Governor General Johannes van den Bosch proposed the Cultivation System, under which Javanese villages were to grow export crops to meet their land tax; in practice the growing became compulsory. It brought the Netherlands large profits, 19 to 32 percent of state revenues from the 1830s to 1860, while rice shortages, famines and epidemics appeared by the 1840s.

uncertainty.note: Furnivall's chapter is titled 1830-1850; the Library of Congress text speaks of profits to 1860 and population figures to 1870.

as_recorded.value: Starting in 1830, a set of policies known as the Cultivation System

importance.justification: A colonial export-crop regime that financed the Netherlands at heavy cost to Javanese villagers.

audience_note: Describes compulsory cultivation, famine and epidemics among Javanese villagers.
